Category: Luxury • Fabrication: DV29 - 5,000eb - 1 Month

Humanity Loss: 14 (4d6) • Install: Hospital

Discontinued in 2069 after a flood of reports detailing its poor interface with neural processors and prefrontal cortexes, these extremely rare arm implants are some of the best Mantis Blade models ever designed. The synth-muscles are faster, synaptic responses more intense, the bloodthirst more fervent, and lethality extremely evident.

Iconic Paired Cyberarm Options. Requires Paired Cyberarms and 2 Cyberarm Option Slots on each Cyberarm. Counts as 2 installations of Borgware. Each arm now has a One-Handed Excellent Quality Heavy Melee Weapon that can be successfully concealed without a Check and can be drawn and stowed without an Action. While the weapon is “popped up,” the user can’t hold anything in that arm’s hand. While both blades are “popped up,” the user can wield both blades as a single EQ ROF 2 Very Heavy Melee Weapon with a 4m/yds range and can negate the normal movement penalty for climbing.

Whenever either of these blades inflicts a Critical Injury, the user rolls three times on the Critical Injury table and chooses their favorite option for the victim to suffer. If the user has currently active Speedware and a total Initiative Bonus of +4 or higher, when rolling for damage with these blades, any damage die that land on a 1 are re-rolled until they result in a higher value.

Fabrication: DV29 - 5,000eb - 1 Month
Type: Cyberarm
Install: Hospital
Option Slots: uses 2

Foundry notes:

  • Iconic: it can't be bought or sourced on the street, can't be fabricated without its Blueprint, can't be taken during Character Generation, and once acquired can't be destroyed unless the player agrees to it beforehand.
  • The price is the Luxury benchmark, for working out repairs and Tech Upgrades. Iconics can't be bought.
  • One item for the pair, as Corgo installs them together. Its size is the 2 slots it takes in one arm; it needs 2 in each.
  • Counts as two installations of Borgware for Maximum Humanity Loss, applied by hand.
  • Cyberware items have no Quality field, so the Excellent Quality is in the text only.

From Corgo's 77 Collection V3 by Corgopolis (Becoming Iconic > Iconic Cyberware).
